title: AWS Lambda consumers for Apache Kafka with OAuth and IAM authentication (Node.js)
description: Three Node.js AWS Lambda functions with Apache Kafka event sources that authenticate with IAM on Amazon MSK, OAuth through Amazon Cognito, or OAuth with tokens issued by AWS IAM.

introBox.headline: How it works
text: This collection contains three patterns. Each deploys a Kafka cluster and an Amazon EC2 client instance with AWS CloudFormation, then an AWS Lambda function with an Apache Kafka event source with AWS SAM or the AWS CLI.

Amazon MSK with IAM authentication: the event source mapping signs each connection with the function's execution role (IAM_AUTH), and IAM policies authorize access to the cluster, topic, and consumer group.

Self-managed Apache Kafka with SASL/OAUTHBEARER through an external OAuth 2.0 provider (Amazon Cognito): the event source mapping obtains access tokens with the client credentials grant (OAUTHBEARER_AUTH).

Self-managed Apache Kafka with SASL/OAUTHBEARER using tokens issued by AWS IAM: through IAM outbound identity federation, the event source mapping obtains a web identity token for the function's execution role (IAM_OAUTHBEARER_AUTH), with no identity provider or secret.
In every pattern the function decodes each Kafka record, logs it to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, and writes its fields to Amazon DynamoDB.
For detailed deployment instructions, see the README.md of each pattern.
